pageCache.text:
Reach Academy Hanworth Park’s vision is that every single pupil will leave us with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.
Welcome
A warm welcome to Reach Academy Hanworth Park, an all-through free school in west London.
We opened the doors to our first Reception and Year 7 pupils in September 2024 along with our founding team of teachers and support staff. Since then, we have welcomed a Reception and Year 7 cohort every September and continue to grow. We have seen amazing progress from our fantastic pupils and look forward to seeing our school flourish even more in the years to come.
Our site is adjacent to our sister school, Reach Academy Feltham (RAF), and our entrance is currently on Feltham High Street, to the right side of RAF. As our school grows, we will transfer into a bigger building next door. Together we are part of the Academy Trust: Reach Schools, which is based at 53-55 High Street, Feltham, TW13 4AB.
At Reach Academy Hanworth Park, we have created a warm supportive community where every child is truly known and helped to realise their potential. We are deliberately a small school, with only 90 pupils per year, so that we build strong relationships.
Our school is a community of care, kindness and excellent learning, built on genuine mutual respect. Why not join us as our school grows in our shared vision of ensuring that every child goes on to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity?
Louis Everett and Kirsty SimkinCo-headteachers
Our vision
“Every single pupil will leave us with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.”

Are you interested in your child joining our fantastic school community? Why not come to one of our Open Events this autumn? These are for families and children who are starting school in September 2027 or are in Year 6 this September. Please book in advance by clicking the fliers below if you’re interested in your child joining us as spaces are limited. We very much look forward to meeting you then!

The admissions deadline for Reception admissions is 15th January 2027.

For Educators

You’ll be given access to exclusive content, blogs, updates on events, and our latest vacancies. We look forward to seeing you soon!
Join us
Reach Schools believe in the importance and impact of genuine relationships, a united community and excellent teaching.
Why Reach Academy Hanworth Park?
A unique opportunity
We are creating and building a community that best serves the needs of pupils to help them go on to live a life of choice and opportunity.
Built on success
We’re taking all we’ve learnt from our first Reach School, Reach Academy Feltham, to deliver excellent education and support.
Part of the community
We meet our pupils and their families ahead of them starting school at Reach Academy Hanworth Park as part of our commitment to developing long lasting relationships with our community.
In the heart of Feltham
Reach Academy Hanworth Park is located on Feltham High Street, right next to Reach Academy Feltham and is currently housed in fantastic purpose built accommodation. The building has an art room, science laboratory, libraries, classrooms and playgrounds for our growing cohorts of pupils. Click the button below to see where our pupils learn, play and have fun!
Meanwhile our brand new, state of the art school is being constructed close to our school site and is due to open in 2027.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reach values - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Reach values
Explore the significance of each of the ‘Reach’ letters
At Reach Academy Hanworth Park, we confidently demonstrate our Reach values – a central theme across all Reach Schools. We explore these five pillars, making sure each value gets its own spotlight at least every half term. We don’t just teach these values, we cheer them on with vibrant messaging and displays, meaningful teaching moments, assemblies, and celebrations for those who exercise them.
We won’t just keep these successes to ourselves, we will announce them to our student’s families, and make sure our community is also celebrating these all-important traits. Each one is thoughtfully crafted to arm our students with everything they need to lead lives full of choice and opportunity.
Our core values
Reflect
‘Reflect’ embodies a core value at Reach Academy Hanworth Park because we believe in the power of constant learning from ourselves and others. It’s about taking a moment to think before we act, learning from our mistakes, and understanding ourselves at a deeper level. This reflective practice cultivates self-awareness and fosters personal growth.
Endeavour
Endeavouring or working hard is another value we uphold. At Reach Schools, we subscribe to the idea that success is the product of hard work, not luck. We pour 100% of our effort into everything we do, whether it’s tackling academic challenges or finding solutions to problems. We embrace the ethos that our dedication and industriousness are the keys to achievement.
Aspire
Aspiration is a driving force at Reach Schools. We dare to dream, and we instill the bravery in our students to make those dreams a reality. This involves cultivating self-belief and, at times, leading others towards a shared vision. When we aspire, we encourage ourselves to plan for greatness, believe in our abilities, and guide others on the journey.
Show Courage
Showing courage, perhaps one of the most challenging values to live by, is integral to our school’s ethos. Whether it’s revealing our weaknesses or strengths, we encourage our students to embrace vulnerability and risk. We teach them to not fear making mistakes, to persist in the face of adversity, and to think creatively. This courage forms the bedrock of resilience and innovation.
Have fun
Finally, ‘Have Fun‘ is a value that encapsulates our belief in the joy of learning. When exploring the other values, having fun comes naturally. But sometimes, we also need to relax and have fun to get the most out of the other values. We foster an environment where students are passionate about what they do, show kindness to themselves and others, and work well in teams. This value reminds us that whilst education is about academic success, it’s also about enjoying the journey and supporting each other along the way.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
About us
Find out about Reach Academy Hanworth Park and all that we aim to achieve.
Built on success
Building on the continued success of Reach Academy Feltham, our school serves the same mission — to ensure that every single pupil will leave us with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity. We are taking all that we’ve learned about excellent teaching, strong relationships and community values into everything we do at Reach Academy Hanworth Park. The school is part of the Academy Trust: Reach Schools, which is based in the heart of the community in Feltham.
A unique opportunity
Reach Academy Hanworth Park opened with a Reception and Year 7 cohort in September 2024 and every year we welcome another 90 children into these year groups.
Starting small means families get to know our teachers, as we journey together through many exciting milestones in the lives of our pupils.
Teachers and team members have access to frequent career development and training, as well as opportunities for growth.
Part of the community
Reach Schools are passionate about the borough of Hounslow which is why we’ve carefully chosen the location of our new school! As we welcome new pupils, we make sure to visit families in person to explain all that we have to offer, and commit to welcome events and community social events throughout the year. We value young people and their families from pre-school to post-school and continue to partner with local organisations to provide the best care. Contact: Reach Schools, 53-55 High Street, Feltham, TW13 4AB, info@reachacademy.org.uk and 020 8831 1620.

Our co-headteachers
Meet Louis and Kirsty
“We’re delighted to be the Co-headteachers of Reach Academy Hanworth Park, which opened in September 2024.
Building on the continued success of Reach Academy Feltham, our school serves a shared vision, to ensure that:
Every single pupil will leave us with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.“
Before becoming Co-headteacher in 2026, Kirty worked as an Assistant Headteacher at Reach Academy Hanworth Park since it opened in September 2023. She brings a combination of strategic clarity with warmth, energy and an unwavering commitment to the Reach vision.
Kirsty graduated from the University of Oxford with a BA in Biological Sciences. Before becoming a teacher, she worked as a research assistant on marine conservation projects in Madagascar and Australia. Kirsty completed her teacher training through the Teach First programme. She joined Reach Academy in 2017 and has worked as a teacher and in middle and senior leadership. Outside school, Kirsty is always on the lookout for her next adventure, be that between the pages of a book or underneath the sea with her scuba-gear.
With many years of senior leadership experience in education across West London, Louis brings that fantastic experience to Reach Schools.
Louis graduated from the University of Hull with a degree in History before completing a Masters in Education whilst training to be a teacher at the University of Cambridge. Louis is passionate about the power of comprehensive education and has a track record of excellence in schools in Suffolk and London. This breadth of experience has led to Louis working with the Department for Education on curriculum and online learning as well as speaking on a range of educational topics at national conferences. He lives in Acton with his wife Laura and his daughter.
Interested in joining Louis and Kirsty?
As a relatively new school, every year we are growing in pupils, and therefore need more fantastic teachers. Why not join our exciting journey?

pageCache.pageTitle: Reach's Language Superstars - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Reach’s Language Superstars
Reach Schools’ pupils have been recognised internationally and nationally for their outstanding language skills.
Youngest A* ever in Sanskrit?
Lakshmi from Reach Academy Hanworth Park has been honoured by the Indian High Commission in London for receiving an A* in Sanskrit iGCSE aged just thirteen. Lakshmi has been learning the subject in her own time over the past three years and had to teach herself the script before learning to understand the language.
Lakshmi, her parents and Co-headteacher Louis Everett travelled to meet the High Commissioner and be congratulated. She has also received a Certificate of Appreciation by the High Commission of India in recognition of her outstanding achievements.
Lakshmi’s parents said:
‘We are incredibly proud of our daughter for receiving this wonderful recognition. To see our daughter connect so well with Sanskrit, and achieve this level of knowledge at such an early age is extraordinary.”
Co-headteacher Louis Everett said:
“What Lakshmi has achieved is extraordinary. Sanskrit is an incredibly complex and difficult language to learn. To achieve the very top grade is a phenomenal feat in itself but Lakshmi has achieved this whilst continuing to perform strongly in all her academic subjects and engaging in a range of creative arts and sporting enrichment.”
Commendations for Translation Skills
At Reach Academy Feltham, three pupils were highly commended by the Anthea Bell Prize for Young Translators. Pupils at the school submitted a total of nineteen translations in four different languages to the Prize.
Danyal Kazmi (17) received two high commendations for Mandarin and Spanish, Alice Valcheva (12) was highly commended for Russian, while Rawan Adam (17) was highly commended for French.
More than 25 thousand young people took part in this national competition recognising creative translation. It is open to pupils aged 11-18 at schools across the UK and is run by the University of Oxford’s Queen’s College. The prize is named after Anthea Bell OBE (1936–2018) who is considered one of the leading literary translators of the 20th and 21st centuries.
Head of Languages at Reach Academy Feltham, Chloe Sides said:
“I am incredibly proud of all of our linguists who took part in the Anthea Bell Translation Prize and want to congratulate Danyal, Rawan and Alice who have been awarded a commendation in such a highly respected competition. What an achievement! At Reach, we truly value languages, ensuring that all of our pupils are able to sit a GCSE in at least one language (with many choosing to do two or even three). Our students know that the skills and knowledge developed through language study will lead to a life of choice and opportunity which is why we are so pleased to run A-level language study through the Languages For All programme.”

Become a school governor
Support our leaders and shape our school’s provision for students
We are currently looking for volunteers to become governors at Reach Academy Hanworth Park!
To prepare for the opening of our new school, we are looking for volunteers to form the founding local governing body which will play a fundamental role in supporting and challenging executive leaders as they shape provision for children and young people at Reach Academy Hanworth Park.
This is an exciting and unique opportunity to play a crucial role in the development of a brand new school and to have a significant impact on the local community.
Taking part in the governance of a school will be challenging but also hugely rewarding and benefit you in several ways. Here’s why you might want to volunteer for these roles:
To learn more about the role and the skills and attributes we are looking for, please read the job pack below.
We are committed to an ethos of diversity and inclusion throughout our organisation. We would particularly welcome applications for governor roles from candidates from underrepresented backgrounds.
For more information please read our recruitment pack:
If you would like to apply, please send your CV and a cover email, including 250 words explaining why you wish to apply to be a member of the Local Governing Body and what makes you suitable for the role. Applications should be sent to to anna.machin@reachacademy.org.uk by 26th September 2025.
If you have any questions please get in touch with Jenny (above), we would be delighted to have a conversation with you about the role.
We look forward to hearing from you!

pageCache.pageTitle: Our curriculum - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum
We are proud of our intentional curriculum and careful planning.
Our intentional and carefully planned curriculum drives progress to excellent outcomes through establishing a powerful knowledge base and a life-long love of learning.
As an all-through school, Reach Academy Hanworth Park’s curriculum is underpinned by the knowledge, skills and attitudes that are required to achieve academic excellence in each subject at A Level and beyond. Subject leaders and teachers plan backwards from this point.
This ensures that pupils in each phase receive a rigorous, coherent and intelligently sequenced curriculum, which builds on what has come before. Based on our successful model at Reach Academy Feltham, the curriculum at Reach Academy Hanworth Park is grounded in the strongest available evidence about how pupils learn and retain knowledge in the long term – focusing in particular on research from cognitive science.
“We want our pupils to love learning, create lifelong memories and be taught excellent lessons every day.”
— Louis Everett, co-headteacher
Curriculum principles:
The table below summarises the core principles of our curriculum:
Backwards planned and deliberately sequenced
Long term curriculum maps are all-through in design
Knowledge rich, embedding key knowledge deeply and durably
100% sheets – expertly designed which detail specific knowledgeEmbedded process for retrieval practice tests in all curriculum areasExplicit instruction and deliberate practiceHomework policies strongly aligned through KIPP
Carefully resourced with high quality, detailed materials
100% sheets -clarity on what needs to be learnt to all stakeholdersBookletsSlides – simple, dual coding
Aspirational, inclusive and diverse in content
Considered curriculum choices around academic, but diverse and inclusive BLM response – curriculum review
Rigorously assessed and promotes rapid progress
Ongoing formative assessmentFactual recall quizzesSummative assessments and PPM meetings
Thoughtfully and regularly evaluated and reflected upon
Curriculum changes for 2025-26 e.g. homework policies, Pupil Progress Meetings
Our subject overviews
We offer a range of subjects to all ages. As an all-through school, we’re able to provide an extensive education that spans many years. Browse our A-Z of subject overviews below.
Please note that parents and carers have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Studies. Please contact the Co-headteacher if you wish to exercise this right. For more information about our curriculum please contact rahpinfo@reachacademy.org.uk
Phases
Pupils at Reach Academy Hanworth Park are organised into ‘phases’, as outlined below:
Phases refer to the educational and physical organisation of pupils as each floor of the school building will ‘house’ a phase. This ensures that for much of the school day, pupils spend their time learning and socialising with pupils of a similar age, creating a more graduated progression through the school.
Phase 1: Reception to Year 2
Phase 2: Years 3-5
Phase 3: Years 6-8
Phase 4: Years 9-11
Phase 5: Years 12-13
EYFS
At Reach Schools, the children in Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) are independent and inquisitive learners. Reach Academy Hanworth Park provides children with the best possible start to their education, by equipping them with the knowledge, skills and experiences they need to thrive in later education and beyond.
Building Relationships
EYFS at Reach Academy Hanworth Park is founded on relationships with the child, the family and the rest of the school. We balance time in provision with direct instruction, understanding that each child will need different mixes of this to do their best.
Every child is unique
Every child is unique and their strengths and areas for development are supported and developed with a long term aspirational pathway in mind. Our staff are highly skilled and have a depth of knowledge of child development that drives all the work that we do. We know each child as an individual, helping to drive progress through play, direct instruction and small group work.
Staff receive specific training, which enables them to be highly effective both during carpet sessions and free flow. We know that in the EYFS, we lay important foundations and expectations for pupils and parents about our school. We expect all our pupils to attend school because we know that it is only through attending school that they will benefit most from their early years education.
The EYFS curriculum primarily promotes the development of children in the key areas of learning. These are:
The development of these skills underpins the EYFS curriculum and are taught through a combination of modelling, high quality interactions and a carefully planned curriculum. The curriculum contains two strands: the Knowledge strand and the Skills strand. Throughout Reception, Reach Schools ensure that the EYFS curriculum is delivered through a combination of age-appropriate carpet sessions, carefully planned provision and close work and communication with parents. We believe that a balance between direct instruction and play is key to enable the development of the whole child.
As the children progress through the EYFS, their day becomes more structured. This structure provides opportunities to enable them to practise skills and embed knowledge in order to ensure a smooth transition into Key Stage One.
Please click on the button above or here to find our more about our Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum, including information about our Read, Write Inc Phonics scheme.
Communication and language
Personal, social and emotional development
Physical development
Subjects
At Phases 1-3, pupils are taught the following subjects:
Food Technology / DT
At Phase 4 for GCSE, pupils will typically study 8-10 subjects, including English Literature/Language, Maths and Double/Triple Science. In Years 10-11, pupils study RE short course, Core PE and Team Reach (PSHE).
Health and Social Care
Philosophy / Religious Studies

Enrichment
We offer a range of fantastic experiences for all our pupils to learn and have fun!
Enrichment
Every Friday during period 6, our pupils finish lessons early to enjoy ‘enrichment’. Teachers run these fantastic sessions so that our young people can enjoy opportunities they may not find elsewhere.
Pupils who have worked hard and shown the Reach values over the week who have scored over 75 on their payslips enjoy enrichment in either computing, poetry, drama, sports and history. Every term we rotate what is on offer so that every pupil has the chance to take part in the range of opportunities on offer. The pupils really enjoy their Friday enrichment and it is a great way to end the week.
We also offer a wide range of school trips, after school activities, music lessons, sports fixtures and every year put on a fantastic musical production. Click below and scroll down for more information.
After School Clubs
At Reach Academy Hanworth Park we have a range of after school clubs that run almost everyday after school. These clubs allow our pupils to experience new sports, spend more time learning about subjects they are interested in, or learn brand new and vital skills such as debating.
The clubs we currently offer include netball, football, debating, maths, history and politics, science, JAM coding and board games.
Every Monday and Wednesday morning before school, there is a sports club for pupils who want to start the day in an active way. During this club we focus on sports that we don’t currently cover on the curriculum to introduce them to an even wider range of sports. We have played badminton, basketball, rounders and cricket so far. The pupils really endeavour to work hard even in the early mornings!
Schools’ sports competitions
We play regular fixtures against other schools in a combined team called Reach Schools with Reach Academy Feltham. We have a number of football and netball matches against local schools which pupils thoroughly enjoy.
We have also started inter-schools competitions, participating in netball and football against Reach Academy Feltham. The pupils have shown fantastic sportsmanship and teamwork throughout these matches.
We encourage everyone to join a club to help their physical, social and mental wellbeing. We know that regular exercise has great benefits for a child’s academic progress as well as their mental health.
Inter-form competitions
After the pupils learn about a sport, they compete in an inter-from competition during lunch time. This gives everyone the chance to win a trophy for their form.
So far we have held handball, netball and gymnastics competitions, which have been great fun for them to play and for staff to referee and judge.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care for Primary children
Our pre-school and after-school cares
Kid Space @Reach
Busy parents sometimes need the flexibility of a longer day…and children love it too!
Reach School’s wraparound care means that you can relax knowing that your child is in safe hands and having fun until you are ready to collect them.
We provide a breakfast club between the hours of 7.30am and the start of school. Children can have breakfast to fuel their day, play games, draw/colour in, or relax in a quiet area before the day ahead. We believe that good food supports children in learning and going on to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity. Breakfast club is £3 from 7.30am for a full session until the start of your child’s day. The children will go directly to their classroom after breakfast club.
Reach Academy Hanworth Park is part of the national rollout of the government’s ‘free breakfast clubs programme’ which gives children a soft start to the day, helping them feel ready to learn. This means we are able to provide a free breakfast to all children from Reception-Year 2 for 30 minutes prior to the start of the school day. Parents must still book this via My Child At School so that we know how many children to expect and children must be dropped off between 8.20-8.25am via the primary side gate. Children arriving after this time will not be able to join.
During our after school care between the end of the day and 6pm, children can get involved in playing a wide range of activities such as sports, arts and crafts, team games, ICT and much more. Traditional toys such as dolls, cars, lego, dress up clothes and board games are also on offer. We believe that encouraging children to explore a variety of skills and hobbies supports them in broadening their horizons and choices in life.
Full session after school – 6pm (snack provided)
Short session after school – 4.30pm (no snack provided)
4.30pm- 6pm (for children booked into a club, snack provided)
7.30am breakfast club early start session

Priority Admissions Criteria – pupils eligible for the pupil premium
The pupil premium grant provides funding to improve educational outcomes for disadvantaged pupils in state-funded schools in England.
Who is eligible for pupil premium?
Pupils who are, or have been, eligible for FSM over the last 6 years are part of the ‘Ever 6’ FSM cohort. This is used for disadvantage funding and accountability purposes. Following the expansion of FSM, Ever 6 FSM will be based on targeted FSM only.
From the start of the 2026 to 2027 academic year, the Department for Education (DfE) is delivering an expansion to FSM eligibility to include all pupils from households in receipt of Universal Credit. There will then be 2 categories of FSM:
Targeted FSM, which continues to be based on the existing £7,400 income thresholdExpanded FSM, which will apply to meals only, covering pupils who do not qualify for Targeted FSM, but who are in households in receipt of Universal Credit
Following the expansion of FSM, only pupils eligible for Targeted FSM will be part of the Ever 6 FSM cohort. This means that pupils who become eligible for FSM for the first time through the new Expanded FSM category will not attract pupil premium funding.Pupils who were eligible for FSM before the expansion will continue to be part of the Ever 6 FSM cohort after the expansion. That includes any pupil whose household income increases after the expansion, such that they either lose FSM eligibility altogether or become eligible for FSM through Expanded FSM. Such pupils will remain part of the Ever 6 FSM cohort for 6 years.
How do I know I am eligible for pupil premium?
Children from households in receipt of Universal Credit with annual household earnings of £7,400 or less (the existing threshold for FSM prior to the expansion), will be eligible for targeted FSM. In addition to receiving free meals, pupils eligible for targeted FSM will attract pupil premium and other disadvantage funding for their schools.
Pupil premium and other disadvantage funding is currently allocated in respect of pupils who are recorded in school census returns as eligible for FSM, or have been recorded as eligible for FSM in the past 6 years (referred to as Ever 6 FSM). From the start of the 2026 to 2027 academic year, Ever 6 FSM will be based on targeted FSM. This cohort is also used for accountability purposes.
Free School Meals and Pupil Premium
For families of existing pupils who wish to apply for Free School Meals, due-to a change in circumstances, you will need to complete the form with LGFL: https://fsm.lgfl.net/
If submitting an in-year transfer from another school, you can provide a letter from your child’s current school which states that your child is eligible for Pupil Premium, and is eligible for targeted Free School Meals, as supporting evidence. This should have the start date that your child became eligible and an end date if applicable.

Reading
How we celebrate and develop a love of reading in school
Reading is key to your child’s success
At Reach Academy Hanworth Park, we believe that reading is the key to your child’s future success. Research shows that pupils who read regularly go on to achieve better exam results, have more choices in life and even feel happier. Pupils in all year groups should be reading for at least 30 minutes per day.
Reading expectations
All pupils at Reach Academy Hanworth Park are expected to read widely outside of the school day. Our expectation is that pupils are reading three things at any given time:
A specified fiction book which we will provide you with. Please see more about our reading scheme below.Year 7 Reading SchemeYear 8 Reading SchemeYear 9 Reading Scheme
A book your child chooses independentlyThis can include books they have already read, graphic novels or books aimed at younger children. Recommended Reading for Year 7 Recommended Reading for Year 8Recommended Reading for Year 9
Some kind of non-fiction text which could include a book, newspaper or magazine. See our Recommended Reading lists for a range of great options.
Supporting your child with reading at home
Children are more likely to read and enjoy reading if their parents/carers show them that reading is important.
You can help them do this in the following ways:

At Reach Academy Hanworth Park there is a vast range of support available to pupils during their time with us. We strive to ensure all pupils are happy, healthy and safe and achieving their full potential.
A supportive practice is embedded throughout Reach Academy Hanworth Park; we ensure every child is supported and encouraged to be the best they can be at every level; from making sure they are organised for their lessons and the day ahead, or supporting them in making sure they are taking the right options and choices for Year 10. Our pupil support provision also offers a number of interventions for pupils who need additional support:
Safeguarding Concerns
At Reach Academy Hanworth Park, we strive to make sure all our students are safe in school, at home, online and in the community. It is every staff member’s responsibility to ensure our students are safe and secure and to promote their personal safety and well-being. If a child makes a disclosure of any form of abuse we have a legal duty to act upon this information. It is standard procedure to inform the local authority of this disclosure and to seek advice and guidance. It is best practice to inform parents and carers of the disclosure, however in some instances we are advised not to by children’s services and they will contact parents/carers directly. We appreciate that this can be a particularly difficult circumstance to deal with and we commit to support families as a unit to ensure everyone is safe and happy.
Please see our safeguarding policy for more detailed information on our procedures.
Legislation
Keeping children Safe in Education
Working together to safeguard children
Worried about a child?
If you are concerned about a child at, please email/contact our Trust Safeguarding Lead: georgia.strong@reachacademy.org.uk or Reach Academy Hanworth Park’s Deputy Safeguarding Lead, co-headteacher: louis.everett@reachacademy.org.uk or telephone 020 8831 1620 or Hounslow Children’s services – on 020 8583 6600 option 2
If you are contacting us out of hours (before 8am and after 5pm) you can contact:
Hounslow duty team 020 8583 2222 and ask to speak to the duty social worker or the NSPCC helpline for support and advice for free – call on or contact NSPCC online.
In an emergency please call 999 or in a non-emergency call 101.
Relationships matter
We build strong relationships with pupils and their parents. This begins with a home visit, which enables us to have a breadth of information about every child in our school. These relationships, founded on trust, allow for open and honest dialogue and we make it clear with parents that we are a team, working together to have challenging conversations.
Our Place2Be service provides mental health support through one -to-one counselling using tried and tested methods backed by research. A drop-in service is also available.
We use CPOMs to report concerns and track everything so as not to miss anything which may impact every single child being able to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity.
We have employed a Family Support Worker since the school opened in 2012 and have been instrumental in initiating the SHEL programme (School-Home Engagement Leads) across Hounslow. We also designed and lead the CAPP (Community Action Partnership Panel) which brings together cross-school safeguarding teams and police to ensure better joint working and problem-solving.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our approach - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Our approach
What makes the way we work effective and enjoyable?
A small school
Reach Academy Hanworth Park will have 90 students in each year group—from Nursery all the way to Year 11.This means we’re big enough to maintain an expert staff team with a wide range of specialisms. It also means we’re small enough to develop strong and lasting relationships and a deep understanding of the individual needs of every child and their family.
With big ambitions
We’re here to help realise the aspirations and achievements of every child. Our vision is that every pupil at Reach Academy Hanworth Park will achieve academic success and have the opportunity to thrive and succeed in life beyond school. It’s our job, in partnership with families, to chart a clear path to success for every child in our care.
We prioritise relationships
We arrange the school day to ensure that staff and students form excellent relationships. We invest heavily in training to ensure our school community is calm, supportive and boundaried. We employ expert practitioners to support the mental and physical well-being of our staff, pupils and their families.
Develop excellent teachers
We know that a great teacher is the single biggest factor in determining excellent pupil outcomes. We invest heavily in thinking about what great teaching and learning look like, and how we support our teachers to get better every day.
Leading an all-through curriculum
We have developed a rigorous, carefully sequenced, cross-phase curriculum to ensure consistency and coherence throughout our students’ educational journey. Pupils’ knowledge builds cumulatively during their time with us—with teachers able to establish clear links with topics and concepts studied in other subjects and in previous years.
The all-through nature of our school enables all children to access specialist teachers and resources from a young age.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our beliefs - Reach Academy Hanworth Park
pageCache.text:
Our beliefs
Explore the five pillars that are prioritised across Reach Schools.
Here are five things that matter to us and our commitments to you.
Reach Schools believe that relationships, leadership, rigour, coherence, and community are key to a healthy learning environment. When placed at the centre of our schools, they provide health, stability and success. We commit to these pillars in all Reach Schools and prioritise them at every level of the organisation.
Community matters
We believe in our community.
We commit to working in partnership with our school community; identifying, celebrating and harnessing what’s great about where we live to improve outcomes for all of our children.
Relationships matter
We believe in the transformational power of relationships.
We commit to establishing, nurturing and valuing strong, trusting relationships throughout our school community.
Coherence matters
We believe in the power of ‘all-through’ education.
We commit to providing a coherent educational experience for every child—securing a clear pathway to a life of choice and opportunity.
Rigour matters
We strive for excellence in everything we do.
We commit to always reflecting critically, seeking feedback, thinking creatively and acting intentionally in our pursuit of excellence.
Leadership matters
We embrace our role as community leaders.
We commit to advocating for all of the children in our care—doing whatever it takes to secure a life of choice and opportunity for all.
We empower our children by actively teaching them how to speak up and advocate for themselves and others.
